text:
The Canucks arrive in Edmonton winless in four (0-4-0) after a 6-2 loss at Winnipeg, and they're 1-4-0 in their last five, with Filip Chytil on injured reserve. Elias Pettersson has taken his spot beside Jonathan Lekkerimäki and Brock Boeser. The Oilers dropped a 5-4 game to Anaheim two days ago but are 3-1-1 in their last five, and Isaac Howard is out. Zach Hyman could return.

The chance numbers lean Edmonton. At five on five, EDM has taken 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and VAN 41%, and our model projects 3.63 goals for the Oilers to 2.54. Edmonton's results are running ahead of its chances, with finishing doing the lifting. Its power play creates 0.88 expected goals a game, and VAN's penalty kill allows 0.91, while the Canucks take 4.2 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Leevi Meriläinen (VAN) and Devon Levi (EDM) are both below expected this season, at -1.74 and -1.25 goals saved above expected. Meriläinen was 17.93 goals worse than expected last year, and Levi has no figure from last season.

Connor McDavid carries a 17-game point streak and a 95% chance at a point, and Leon Draisaitl has 51% to score. For Vancouver, Boeser has 7 points in 6 games against Edmonton. Our under-the-radar pick is Kasperi Kapanen (EDM), at 50% for a point against a season-pace 39%, with his ice time up and the Canucks allowing the second-most expected goals per 60.
